subject: Integration exception & prioritized feature gaps for CloudHub listing
messages:
From: Jenna Park <j.park@cloudhub.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: CloudHub listing: items that need exceptions / compatibility notes

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for hopping on the call yesterday. Attached is our consolidated marketplace requirements doc (marketplace_requirements_v2.pdf) — it highlights a handful of things that are outside of Redwood's standard listing pre-reqs and will need either an exception or an engineering workaround. High-level asks: 

- Telemetry retention: CloudHub requires 13 months retention for audit logs for customers in our financial vertical; your standard hosting only exposes 90 days.
- Regional routing: We need guaranteed routing through us-east or eu-west for a subset of customers during launch.
- Runtime compatibility: Our onboarding automation expects the inference runtime to expose a /health/kv endpoint for prefix cache checks (not listed in your public docs).

Can your team confirm which of these are realistic as exceptions vs roadmap items? We are targeting a soft listing in the CloudApp store in Q1; if exceptions are required we need to lock them this month.

Attached: marketplace_requirements_v2.pdf (PDF) — see appendix B for compliance ask matrix.

Are you available for a 30-min sync tomorrow (11/21) to triage?

Best,
Jenna Park
Partnerships PM — CloudHub
j.park@cloudhub.com

Thanks Jenna — looping in product (Priya), partner eng (Karthik) and our partner ops lead (Jonas) to triage. Quick read of the doc, and a few clarifying questions so we can scope work and decide exception vs roadmap: 

1) Telemetry retention: is the 13-month requirement applied per-tenant or aggregated at CloudHub-level? If per-tenant we need to evaluate storage/cost implications and whether Dedicated or Private deployment is required.
2) Regional routing: are you asking for hard region pinning per customer or just a preferred routing policy with fallback?
3) Runtime /health/kv: can you share the exact request/response shape you expect for the prefix cache check? That will determine whether this is a small surface addition or a breaking API change.

I've attached a very quick gap template (initial_gap_analysis.xlsx) — can you fill the shaded columns for priority and acceptance criteria? That will help Priya prioritize.

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik: quick compatibility assessment and list of technical blockers (ETA 11/22).
- Priya: prioritize features vs exception path (ETA 11/23).
- Jonas + I: coordinate commercial/ops implications and draft exception doc if needed.

I can take the 11/21 slot at 10am PT; if that works for you I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Partner Success Manager — Redwood Inference

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 9:12 AM Jenna Park <j.park@cloudhub.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for hopping on the call yesterday...

Quick technical readout from Partner Eng:

- Telemetry retention: Redwood hosted (multi-tenant) stores detailed inference telemetry for 90 days by default. Extending to 13 months is feasible but not for multi-tenant by default — two viable paths: (a) Dedicated capacity with extended retention as a config (preferred for predictability), or (b) an export pipeline to CloudHub-managed storage (S3) with signed transfer (we'd need an export schema and retention SLA).
- Regional routing: we currently support preferred-region routing with failover; hard pinning per-tenant is supported only on Dedicated/Private.
- /health/kv endpoint: the runtime exposes an internal KV health check but not over the public API. We can add a lightweight health-check endpoint that returns prefix cache status (200/OK with JSON {"kv_ok": true}) without opening internal caches, but we'd need ~2 sprint work to add and test across supported runtimes.

Estimated effort (rough):
- Runtime health endpoint: 2 sprints (eng 2 FTE) + 1 sprint QA.
- Telemetry export pipeline: 3–4 sprints to build and hardened UX for export + retention config (if we do dedicated, infra + cost modeling needed).

Related Jira: INTG-789 (tracking runtime health endpoint + docs). See minimal compatibility matrix attached.

Recommendation: offer a hybrid path for Q1 listing: allow CloudHub to list Redwood with a documented exception (telemetry/export + preferred-region routing) and a canary program for customers that need 13-month retention. Meanwhile we scope runtime health api into the Q1 roadmap to remove the exception by Q2.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: CloudHub listing: items that need exceptions / compatibility notes

Folks — after reviewing the doc and Karthik's notes, here's my proposed prioritization for what we ship vs what we exception for the CloudHub listing: 

1) Ship (roadmap Q1): runtime health endpoint (/health/kv) — needed for onboarding automation; target delivery by end of Q1.
2) Exception (short-term): telemetry retention to 13 months — offer an export-to-S3 integration as an exception path for CloudHub customers who opt-in; require documented SLAs and opt-in acceptance.
3) Exception (ops): hard region pinning — only available on Dedicated/Private; for listing we call out region-preference with clear fallback.

Action items: 
- Stephanie/ Jonas: draft an "exception playbook" (commercial terms + opt-in flow) for CloudHub and attach to listing.
- Karthik: scope INTG-789 into the Q1 sprint plan and send acceptance criteria by 11/27.
- Legal: we need a short exception addendum; can someone loop in Legal (cc'ed separately) and propose a template?

Jenna — if CloudHub can accept the export opt-in / canary model for initial listing we can proceed without blocking product roadmap commitments.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Marketplace Product Manager — Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

Thanks all — this readout is great and aligns with our commercial needs. CloudHub is comfortable with the canary / export opt-in approach for Q1 listing as long as we have: 

- A clear playbook attached to the listing that explains the opt-in flow and cost expectations.
- An estimated schedule for the runtime /health/kv endpoint (your ETA of end of Q1 works).
- Legal contact for exception addendum — please loop in our counsel (Maya Reddy, m.reddy@cloudhub.com) when you draft.

We are happy to proceed on that basis. Once you have the exception playbook draft, send it to me and I'll get it into our marketplace intake for the listing slot.

Proposed next sync: Tuesday 11/30 10am PT to review the playbook and timeline. Let me know if that works and Stephanie please send invite.
